AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Disease Control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Disease Control.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Disease Control.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Urban and peri-urban Agriculture? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Biotechnology? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Biotechnology.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Biotechnology.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Biotechnology.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Cropping? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Cropping.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Cropping.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Cropping.

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Disease control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Disease control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Disease control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Disease control.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

16. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Urban and peri-urban Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Powered Agricultural Implements and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Agricultural Biotechnology and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Agri- business Accounts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Business and Career Opportunities in Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
